sampling_model.design: The canonical experiment is one observation \(Z_h\sim N(h,\Sigma)\). Transfer from \(P_{n,h}\) is conditional on the nonstandard uniform two-sided experiment-equivalence premise, not on ordinary pointwise local asymptotic normality.
sampling_model.units: The target population is summarized locally by the reduced-form mean \(h\in H\) and the partially identified causal welfare contrast \(U^{\ast}\).
sampling_model.treatment: The rule \(\delta(Z_h)\in[0,1]\) is the fraction or probability assigned to treatment; both deterministic and randomized measurable rules are allowed.
sampling_model.overlap: No propensity-score overlap condition is imposed in the Gaussian endpoint game; feasibility is the nonempty interval \([\ell(h),u(h)]\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: For transfer, \(\widehat Z_n\) is generated by the forward kernel \(K_n\) from the nonstandard two-sided experiment-equivalence premise. A sufficient construction on the standard Borel space \(\mathcal X_n\) uses a measurable statistic \(T_n\) with a uniform Gaussian-pivot error \(a_n\to0\) and an \(h\)-independent reconstruction kernel \(\mathsf R_n\) with uniform reconstruction error \(b_n\to0\); setting \(K_n(x,\cdot)=\delta_{T_n(x)}\) and \(L_n=\mathsf R_n\) gives \(\lambda_n\le a_n+b_n\). A training split constructs \(\widehat{\mathsf G}_n\), including \(\widehat\Sigma_n\), and is required separately to return a member of \(\mathcal G_p\) satisfying \(\mathsf B_{\kappa}\), \(P_{n,h}\)-almost surely for every \(n\) and \(h\in H\); the numerical bounds alone do not imply legal membership. A conditionally independent evaluation split constructs \(\widehat Z_n\), and uniform convergence to zero of the expected conditional total-variation distance from \(N(h,\widehat\Sigma_n)\) implies \(\gamma_n\to0\). The reference \(Q_{n,h}\) has exactly the same \(\widehat{\mathsf G}_n\)-marginal as \(P_{n,h}\), so legality and the numerical bounds hold under both joint laws before the certified selector is run. Primitive error is then measured by \(\alpha_n\), and the decision is computed at a strictly positive certified gap \(\varepsilon_n>0\), with \(\varepsilon_n\to0\) only along the sequence. No rate for \(a_n\), \(b_n\), or \(\lambda_n\) is asserted.

tldr: The new angle asks when asymmetric nonsmooth partial identification makes every minimax treatment rule genuinely multivariate. The proposal preserves the unrestricted measurable-rule saddle theorem, face-complete least-favorable priors, convergent global exchange bounds, and the asymmetric triangular coexistence witness, but moves the theorem-level frontier to a finite curved-score certificate. In two dimensions, exact primal-dual closure for a finite endpoint prior, noncancellation of its analytic Gaussian-mixture score, and one regular zero-set arc with curvature bounded away from zero imply a unique minimax rule and exclude every measurable one-index representation. The answer-open task is to construct an unbalanced rational endpoint prior and outward-rounded interval certificate satisfying these conditions, or prove that no such two-dimensional game exists. The full all-one-index, coexistence, or no-one-index normal-fan classification remains open. Every finite exchange tolerance is strictly positive; limiting tolerances may converge to zero. Feasible transfer is retained only as a conditional secondary corollary under two-sided experiment equivalence, legal bounded game estimation, and joint total-variation approximation, with no named-model or rate claim.

project_justification.gap: Theorem 3 of MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Local is the feasible fully differentiable result. Its Assumption 5(i) imposes convexity and centrosymmetry for directionally differentiable bounds, Theorem 4 supplies selected rules for that limit game, Theorem 5 gives their feasible transfer, and the Conclusion leaves the joint directional-differentiability and non-centrosymmetry regime open. Yata2025Optimal relies on an antipodal modulus pair. MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Decision imposes open-set sign ambiguity and establishes multiplicity without classifying the full unrestricted correspondence; the present primitive class instead uses a weaker pointwise sign-ambiguity condition. AradillasFernandezMontielOleaQiuStoyeTinda2026RobustBayes solves ex-ante \(\Gamma\)-MMR and ex-post \(\Gamma\)-PER under its equation-(2.9) constrained prior class and derives uniqueness, randomization, and linear-index threshold conclusions, but does not solve the unrestricted endpoint-state minimax-regret correspondence or exclude arbitrary measurable one-index rules. The corrected-proof Abstract of ChristensenMoonSchorfheide2026OptimalDecisionRules derives asymptotically optimal discrete-choice rules from a hybrid objective: minimax ambiguity treatment for the partially identified payoff parameter conditional on a point-identified parameter, combined with average-risk minimization for the point-identified parameter. That objective is orthogonal to the exact unrestricted signed-endpoint minimax-regret saddle studied here, and neither objective implies the other.
project_justification.niche: Finite endpoint priors produce analytic differences of Gaussian mixtures. Their global primal-dual gap and local boundary jets are finite objects that can certify properties of the entire unrestricted minimax correspondence, including failure of every scalar-index representation.
project_justification.fill: The project derives unrestricted saddle duality and face-complete dual representatives, then proves that exact finite-prior saddle closure plus a nonvanishing curved Bayes-score boundary yields uniqueness and the no-one-index category. Convergent exchange bounds locate candidate priors, while outward-rounded interval arithmetic closes the global risk inequalities and the local curvature inequalities. The triangular value-\(2/3\) construction remains the coexistence regression test, and the complete normal-fan trichotomy remains answer-open. Conditional feasible transfer is secondary and makes no statistical frontier or rate claim.

related_work: Montiel Olea, Qiu, and Stoye, \cite{MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Decision}, establish multiplicity and qualified failure of linear threshold rules in partially identified treatment choice, but do not exclude every randomized measurable rule based on one linear projection. Montiel Olea, Qiu, and Stoye, \cite{MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Local}, solve the smooth asymmetric and nonsmooth centrosymmetric regimes separately and leave their joint relaxation open; the present compact asymmetric polyhedral class occupies that orthogonal regime, not a superclass of their full Assumption-5 class. Yata, \cite{Yata2025Optimal}, obtains an optimal one-index rule from an antipodal modulus pair under centrosymmetry, providing the positive benchmark that the curved-score certificate can falsify outside symmetry. Aradillas Fernández, Montiel Olea, Qiu, Stoye, and Tinda, \cite{AradillasFernandezMontielOleaQiuStoyeTinda2026RobustBayes}, use the constrained ambiguity specification in their equation (2.9), with a symmetric uniform two-point distribution over the reduced-form parameter and unrestricted compatible conditional distributions, and Theorems 1--2 analyze ex-ante \(\Gamma\)-MMR and ex-post \(\Gamma\)-PER rules with uniqueness, randomization, and linear-index threshold conclusions. Those results are orthogonal to the present unrestricted minimax-regret saddle: Nature here ranges over every signed endpoint state, and the curved-score theorem excludes every arbitrary measurable one-index rule \(g(w^{\top}z)\), not only linear threshold rules. Christensen, Moon, and Schorfheide, \cite{ChristensenMoonSchorfheide2026OptimalDecisionRules}, derive asymptotically optimal discrete-choice rules under partial identification by combining minimax ambiguity treatment for the partially identified payoff parameter conditional on a point-identified parameter with average-risk minimization for that point-identified parameter; this description is anchored to the Abstract of the corrected proof dated 13 March 2026. Their hybrid asymptotic objective and the present exact unrestricted signed-endpoint minimax-regret objective are orthogonal, neither objective implies the other, and the present curved-score result concerns exclusion of every arbitrary measurable one-index rule rather than asymptotic efficiency for learning the point-identified parameter. Tetenov, \cite{Tetenov2012Asymmetric}, derives threshold structure for point-identified asymmetric regret, showing that asymmetry alone does not generate the proposed non-index phenomenon. Teicher, \cite{Teicher1963Mixtures}, supplies finite-normal-mixture identifiability, while Zahm et al., \cite{ZahmEtAl2020Ridge}, formalize ridge functions as measurable functions of linear projections and study gradient diagnostics; neither source links analytic mixture-score geometry to uniqueness of an unrestricted minimax treatment rule. Aradillas Fernández et al., \cite{AradillasFernandezEtAl2025Epsilon}, optimize mixtures over a fixed finite rule menu, and Zhang, Wu, and López, \cite{ZhangWuLopez2010Exchange}, treat convex semi-infinite exchange with finite-dimensional primals. The proposed exchange construction instead preserves the exact measurable-rule Bayes envelope and requests only strictly positive finite tolerances. The deeper scan located no paper giving an exact unbalanced least-favorable endpoint distribution, a curved Gaussian-mixture Bayes boundary, and a global certificate excluding every one-index minimax rule. Hirano and Porter, \cite{HiranoPorter2009}, remain pointwise limit-experiment motivation only; the secondary feasible corollary is explicitly conditional on stronger two-sided and joint total-variation premises.
technical_internal_limitation: The curved-score theorem is a sufficient certificate, not the requested necessary-and-sufficient normal-fan classification. Its global premise must be closed by exact inequalities; a plot or floating-point near-zero gap is insufficient. The value-\(2/3\) triangular witness establishes coexistence, not the no-one-index branch. Face completeness concerns only faces charged by some dual optimum. Exchange iterates use exact restricted-game and worst-state oracles, make no complexity-rate claim, and request a strictly positive tolerance at every finite run; no finite termination at tolerance zero is asserted. The conditional transfer corollary requires two-sided experiment equivalence, legal \(\kappa\)-bounded estimated games, and joint total-variation approximation, none of which follows from ordinary DQM or pointwise LAN.
honest_scope: The theorem-level frontier is exact decision geometry in a two-dimensional compact polyhedral Gaussian endpoint game. The all-saddle theorem and face-complete priors hold in general dimension, the triangular construction certifies coexistence, and the curved-score theorem gives a finite sufficient route to the no-one-index category. The existence of a rational unbalanced witness satisfying that route and the full finite primitive trichotomy are open-ended questions. As a sanity check, the centered antipodal specialization recovers Yata's selected one-index rule, while the compact-polyhedral overlap with Theorem 4 of Montiel Olea--Qiu--Stoye has the identical objective by construction; no containment of their full Assumption-5 class is asserted. Conditional feasible transfer is secondary, has no named-model instantiation or rate claim, and uses only strictly positive finite certificate tolerances tending to zero along a sequence.

assumptions.condition: The set \(H\subset\mathbb R^p\) is a nonempty compact convex polytope with nonempty relative interior in its affine hull.

novel.justification: This is a weaker pointwise sign-ambiguity condition, not the open-set condition in Definition 2 of \cite{MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Decision}. It is realistic when one economically plausible local reduced-form mean has strictly two-sided welfare bounds, including finite-support moment-inequality models with continuous polyhedral endpoint maps; no ambient open set of such means is required.

assumptions.condition: There exist Markov kernels \(K_n\) and \(L_n\) such that \(\lambda_n=\max\{\sup_{h\in H}\lVert K_nP_{n,h}-N(h,\Sigma)\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}},\sup_{h\in H}\lVert L_nN(h,\Sigma)-P_{n,h}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}\}\to0\).

novel.justification: This is an explicit nonstandard high-level premise. Differentiability in quadratic mean or pointwise local asymptotic normality does not imply the displayed compact-\(H\), two-sided total-variation deficiency bound, so feasible transfer is conditional on this stronger equivalence. A self-contained sufficient construction is available on the standard Borel spaces \(\mathcal X_n\): suppose there are a measurable statistic \(T_n\), an \(h\)-independent reconstruction Markov kernel \(\mathsf R_n(\cdot\mid z)\), and deterministic \(a_n,b_n\to0\) such that \[\sup_{h\in H}\left\lVert\mathcal L_{P_{n,h}}(T_n)-N(h,\Sigma)\right\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}\le a_n\] and \[\sup_{h\in H}\left\lVert P_{n,h}-\int \mathsf R_n(\cdot\mid z)\,\mathcal L_{P_{n,h}}(T_n)(dz)\right\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}\le b_n.\] Taking \(K_n(x,\cdot)=\delta_{T_n(x)}\) and \(L_n=\mathsf R_n\), contraction of total variation under \(\mathsf R_n\) and the triangle inequality give \(\lambda_n\le a_n+b_n\to0\). These conditions are uniform Gaussian-pivot approximation plus uniform asymptotic sufficiency and reconstruction; they are not claimed for every regular model and impose no convergence rate.

assumptions.condition: For every \(n\) and \(h\in H\), \(P_{n,h}(\widehat{\mathsf G}_n\in\mathcal G_p)=1\).

novel.justification: A training-sample construction can enforce legal membership by fitting the endpoint coefficients subject to the nonempty-interval and pointwise sign-ambiguity restrictions while maintaining a positive-definite covariance estimate. This is an independent legality requirement: numerical bounds on fitted coefficients do not imply membership in \(\mathcal G_p\).

assumptions.condition: For every \(n\) and \(h\in H\), \(P_{n,h}(\mathsf B_{\kappa}(\widehat{\mathsf G}_n))=1\).

novel.justification: Bounded parameterizations of compact polyhedral endpoint models and covariance estimators with eigenvalues constrained to a fixed compact interval satisfy this condition. It controls the loss envelope and continuity modulus but is separate from legal membership in \(\mathcal G_p\).

assumptions.condition: The joint approximation error satisfies \(\gamma_n=\sup_{h\in H}\lVert\mathcal L_{P_{n,h}}(\widehat Z_n,\widehat{\mathsf G}_n)-Q_{n,h}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}\to0\).

novel.justification: A concrete sufficient construction uses a training split to form \(\widehat{\mathsf G}_n\), including \(\widehat\Sigma_n\), with legal membership and the numerical bounds imposed separately by \(\mathrm{ass:estimated-game-legality}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:estimated-game-kappa-bounds}\), and a conditionally independent evaluation split to form \(\widehat Z_n\). If the conditional Gaussian approximation obeys \[\sup_{h\in H}E_{P_{n,h}}\!\left[\left\lVert\mathcal L_{P_{n,h}}(\widehat Z_n\mid\widehat{\mathsf G}_n)-N(h,\widehat\Sigma_n)\right\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}\right]\to0,\] then the common \(\widehat{\mathsf G}_n\)-marginal and conditional disintegration give \(\gamma_n\) no larger than the displayed quantity, hence \(\gamma_n\to0\). This sample-splitting or stable-construction requirement is independent of the two-sided experiment equivalence in \(\mathrm{ass:uniform-two-sided-experiment-equivalence}\), and neither joint approximation nor numerical boundedness substitutes for legal membership in \(\mathcal G_p\).

definitions.name: Compact polyhedral Gaussian endpoint games \(\mathcal G_p\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal G_p=\{\mathsf G=(H,\Sigma,\ell,u):\mathsf G\text{ satisfies }\mathrm{ass:compact-polyhedral-domain},\mathrm{ass:nondegenerate-gaussian-shift},\mathrm{ass:nonempty-identified-interval},\mathrm{ass:nontrivial-sign-ambiguity}\}\), where \(\ell(h)=\max_{j\in J_-}\{a_j^-+(b_j^-)^{\top}h\}\) and \(u(h)=\min_{k\in J_+}\{a_k^++(b_k^+)^{\top}h\}\).

definitions.name: Compact centered polyhedral subclass \(\mathcal G_p^{\mathrm{cs}}\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal G_p^{\mathrm{cs}}=\{\mathsf G=(H,\Sigma,\ell,u)\in\mathcal G_p:H=-H\text{ and }u(h)=-\ell(-h)\text{ for every }h\in H\}\).

definitions.name: Exact compact-polyhedral overlap with Theorem 4
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal O_p^{(4)}=\{\mathsf G=(H,\Sigma,\ell,u)\in\mathcal G_p^{\mathrm{cs}}:(H,\Sigma,\ell,u)\text{ is exactly the Gaussian mean domain, covariance, and pair of lower and upper directional-derivative endpoint maps entering the cited Theorem 4}\}\). The cited result is Theorem 4 of \cite{MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Local}.

definitions.name: Unrestricted randomized decision space \(\mathcal D\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal D=\{\delta\in L^{\infty}(\lambda^p):0\le\delta\le1\ \lambda^p\text{-almost everywhere}\}\), the positive order interval in the closed unit ball, equipped with \(\sigma(L^{\infty}(\lambda^p),L^1(\lambda^p))\). Its elements are \(\lambda^p\)-almost-everywhere equivalence classes. Whenever \(\delta(z)\) is written, an arbitrary Borel representative is used; because every \(N(h,\Sigma)\) is equivalent to \(\lambda^p\), \(q_{\delta}\), every regret, and every Bayes response are representative-invariant.

definitions.name: Endpoint minimax game
definitions.construction: For \(s=(h,+)\), set \(r_s(\delta)=c_+(h)\{1-q_{\delta}(h)\}\); for \(s=(h,-)\), set \(r_s(\delta)=c_-(h)q_{\delta}(h)\); then \(R(\delta)=\sup_{s\in S}r_s(\delta)\) and \(v=\inf_{\delta\in\mathcal D}R(\delta)\).

definitions.name: Gaussian-mixture Bayes envelope
definitions.construction: For \(\pi\in\Pi\), form \(A_{\pi,+}\), \(A_{\pi,-}\), and \(B_{\pi}=A_{\pi,+}-A_{\pi,-}\); the dual payoff is \(b(\pi)=\int_{\mathbb R^p}\min\{A_{\pi,+}(z),A_{\pi,-}(z)\}\,dz\), and its Bayes responses are exactly the rules with \(\delta(z)=1\) on \(\{B_{\pi}>0\}\), \(\delta(z)=0\) on \(\{B_{\pi}<0\}\), and arbitrary values in \([0,1]\) on \(\{B_{\pi}=0\}\).

definitions.name: Primal and dual optimal correspondences
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal D^{\star}=\{\delta\in\mathcal D:R(\delta)=v\}\) and \(\Pi^{\star}=\{\pi\in\Pi:b(\pi)=v\}\); a pair \((\delta,\pi)\) is a saddle when \(\int r_s(\delta)\,d\pi'(s)\le\int r_s(\delta)\,d\pi(s)\le\int r_s(\delta')\,d\pi(s)\) for every \(\delta'\in\mathcal D\) and \(\pi'\in\Pi\).

definitions.name: Face-complete dual representative
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak F^{\star}\) is the finite collection of lower or upper endpoint faces whose relative interior receives positive mass under some \(\pi\in\Pi^{\star}\); \(\Pi^{\mathrm{fc}}\) consists of the priors in \(\Pi^{\star}\) placing positive mass on the relative interior of every member of \(\mathfrak F^{\star}\) with its endpoint sign.

definitions.name: Full-correspondence indexability trichotomy
definitions.construction: The game lies in \(\mathsf C_{\mathrm{all}}\) when \(\varnothing\ne\mathcal D^{\star}\subseteq\mathcal D_1\), in \(\mathsf C_{\mathrm{co}}\) when both \(\mathcal D^{\star}\cap\mathcal D_1\) and \(\mathcal D^{\star}\setminus\mathcal D_1\) are nonempty, and in \(\mathsf C_{\mathrm{none}}\) when \(\mathcal D^{\star}\cap\mathcal D_1=\varnothing\).

definitions.name: Normal-fan and Gaussian-score classification handle \(\mathscr H_{\mathrm{idx}}\)
definitions.construction: Derive a finite certificate from the covariance-whitened endpoint-face normals, the incidence pattern of faces hit by \(\Pi^{\mathrm{fc}}\), ridge factorization of the Gaussian-mixture scores \(B_{\pi}\), and the annihilator space of bounded perturbations that preserve every binding convolution moment; use it to decide \(\mathsf C_{\mathrm{all}}\), \(\mathsf C_{\mathrm{co}}\), or \(\mathsf C_{\mathrm{none}}\).

definitions.name: Finite rational and interval-arithmetic witness handle \(\mathscr H_{\mathrm{noidx}}\)
definitions.construction: Search over games whose vertices of \(H\), entries of \(\Sigma\), endpoint intercepts, and endpoint normals are rational, and over finite endpoint priors \(\pi\) with rational support points, rational masses, and unequal total masses on the two endpoint signs. Use the Gaussian-mixture Bayes rule \(\delta_{\pi}\). Certify exact saddle closure by a rational number \(q\), a finite rational box partition of \(H\), a finite rational truncation box in \(\mathbb R^2\), outward-rounded interval enclosures, and analytic Gaussian-tail bounds proving \(R(\delta_{\pi})\le q\le b(\pi)\). Certify a genuinely curved boundary on a rational box meeting \(\mathcal Z_{\pi}\) by interval lower bounds away from zero for the score gradient and \( |\mathcal K_{\pi}|\).

definitions.name: Finite curved-score no-index certificate
definitions.construction: For \(p=2\), take a finite endpoint prior \(\pi\in\Pi\), form \(\delta_{\pi}=\mathbf 1\{B_{\pi}>0\}\), the regular boundary \(\mathcal Z_{\pi}\), and the curvature numerator \(\mathcal K_{\pi}\). The certificate consists of the exact inequalities \(R(\delta_{\pi})\le q\le b(\pi)\), a proof that \(B_{\pi}\not\equiv0\), and a nondegenerate arc \(\Gamma\subset\mathcal Z_{\pi}\) on which \(\inf_{z\in\Gamma}\lVert\nabla B_{\pi}(z)\rVert>0\) and \(\inf_{z\in\Gamma}|\mathcal K_{\pi}(z)|>0\).

definitions.name: Unrestricted primal-dual exchange certificate
definitions.construction: Fix a dense sequence in \(S\) and start from a finite \(S_1\subset S\). At iteration \(m\), solve the restricted game against \(S_m\) over all \(\delta\in\mathcal D\), choose a restricted saddle \((\delta_m,\pi_m)\), compute \(L_m=b(\pi_m)\) and \(U_m=R(\delta_m)\), and adjoin both the next point of the dense sequence and an endpoint state attaining \(U_m\). A finite run requests a strictly positive tolerance and stops when \(G_m=U_m-L_m\) is no larger than that tolerance; convergence to zero refers only to the infinite sequence, and no finite termination claim is made at tolerance zero.

definitions.name: Tie-uniform certified selector

statements.statement: For every \(\delta\in\mathcal D\) and \(h\in H\), the supremum of expected regret over \(U^{\ast}\in[\ell(h),u(h)]\) equals \(\max\{c_+(h)[1-q_{\delta}(h)],c_-(h)q_{\delta}(h)\}\). Consequently, Nature loses no value by restricting its pure strategies to \(S=H\times\{+,-\}\).
statements.justification: The reduction identifies the exact adversarial state space and prevents a hidden restriction to hand-picked endpoint pairs.

statements.consumer: Every saddle certificate and every numerical separation oracle operates on the reduced endpoint-state space.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(h\in H\) and write \(q=q_{\delta}(h)\in[0,1]\), where the range follows from \(0\leq\delta\leq1\) in \(\mathrm{def:rule-class}\). If the welfare gain is \(x\), the oracle treats when \(x>0\) and does not treat when \(x<0\). Hence the expected regret of a rule whose treatment probability is \(q\) is
\[
 \rho(x,q)=x_{+}(1-q)+(-x)_{+}q.
\]
This is the definition of regret relative to the better of the two constant actions. On \([0,\infty)\), \(x\mapsto\rho(x,q)=x(1-q)\) is nondecreasing, whereas on \((-\infty,0]\), \(x\mapsto\rho(x,q)=(-x)q\) is nonincreasing as \(x\) increases. Because \(\ell(h)\leq u(h)\) by \(\mathrm{ass:nonempty-identified-interval}\), splitting the interval at zero, with an empty side omitted, gives
\[
 \sup_{x\in[\ell(h),u(h)]}\rho(x,q)
 =\max\bigl\{[u(h)]_{+}(1-q),[-\ell(h)]_{+}q\bigr\}
 =\max\bigl\{c_{+}(h)[1-q_{\delta}(h)],c_{-}(h)q_{\delta}(h)\bigr\}.
\]
The two entries in the last maximum are precisely \(r_{(h,+)}(\delta)\) and \(r_{(h,-)}(\delta)\) by \(\mathrm{def:endpoint-game}\). Taking the supremum over \(h\in H\) therefore gives the same value as taking the supremum over \(S=H\times\{+,-\}\), which proves the reduction without imposing any restriction on \(\delta\).

statements.statement: For every \(\mathsf G\in\mathcal G_p\), minimax equality and attainment hold: \[v=\min_{\delta\in\mathcal D}\max_{s\in S}r_s(\delta)=\max_{\pi\in\Pi}b(\pi).\] The sets \(\mathcal D^{\star}\) and \(\Pi^{\star}\) are nonempty and convex. A pair \((\delta,\pi)\in\mathcal D\times\Pi\) is a saddle if and only if: first, \(\delta\) has the Bayes-response form determined by the sign of \(B_{\pi}\); second, \(r_s(\delta)\le v\) for every \(s\in S\); and third, \(r_s(\delta)=v\) for \(\pi\)-almost every \(s\). The set \(\Pi^{\mathrm{fc}}\) is nonempty. Indeed, if \(\mathfrak F^{\star}\ne\varnothing\), choose for each \(F\in\mathfrak F^{\star}\) a prior \(\pi_F\in\Pi^{\star}\) assigning positive mass to the relative interior of \(F\) with its endpoint sign; the finite uniform convex combination of the \(\pi_F\) belongs to the convex set \(\Pi^{\star}\) and lies in \(\Pi^{\mathrm{fc}}\). If \(\mathfrak F^{\star}=\varnothing\), every prior in the nonempty set \(\Pi^{\star}\) is face-complete. Finally, every \(\delta\in\mathcal D^{\star}\) forms a saddle with every \(\pi\in\Pi^{\star}\).
statements.justification: This is the theorem-level kernel: it gives the value, existence, every saddle, and a face-complete dual representative over all measurable randomized rules in the asymmetric polyhedral regime.
statements.gap: Yata2025Optimal uses an antipodal modulus pair under centrosymmetry. Assumption 5(i) and Theorem 4 of MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Local supply selected rules for a directionally differentiable limit game under convexity and centrosymmetry. The compact asymmetric polyhedral regime is an orthogonal case left open by that source, and the present theorem does not claim to contain its full Assumption-5 class.
statements.consumer: An applied researcher can certify a treatment rule without assuming it is a threshold or selecting one optimizer from a potentially large correspondence.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(\mathsf G\in\mathcal G_p\). All endpoint functions are continuous because each is a finite maximum or minimum of affine functions. Thus \(c_{+}\) and \(c_{-}\) are continuous and bounded on the compact set \(H\), by \(\mathrm{ass:compact-polyhedral-domain}\). Positive definiteness in \(\mathrm{ass:nondegenerate-gaussian-shift}\) implies that every \(N(h,\Sigma)\) has a strictly positive Lebesgue density.

We first establish the compactness and continuity facts used below. Put \(\mu=N(0,\Sigma)\) and
\[
 L_h(z)=\frac{dN(h,\Sigma)}{d\mu}(z)
 =\exp\!\left(h^{\top}\Sigma^{-1}z-\frac12h^{\top}\Sigma^{-1}h\right).
\]
Then \(L_h\in L^2(\mu)\), and \(h\mapsto L_h\) is continuous in \(L^2(\mu)\); both assertions follow by evaluating Gaussian exponential moments. In particular,
\[
 q_{\delta}(h)=\int\delta(z)L_h(z)\,d\mu(z).
\]
Every sequence in \(\mathcal D\) is bounded in the Hilbert space \(L^2(\mu)\). A diagonal extraction against a countable orthonormal basis produces a weakly convergent subsequence. If its weak limit is \(d\), testing against indicators of the sets \(\{d<0\}\) and \(\{d>1\}\), and using weak closedness of closed convex sets, gives \(0\leq d\leq1\) almost everywhere. Since \(\mu\) and \(\lambda^p\) are equivalent, \(d\) represents an element of \(\mathcal D\). Consequently, for every finite collection of states, the corresponding risk-vector set
\[
 \bigl\{(r_{s_1}(\delta),\ldots,r_{s_N}(\delta)):\delta\in\mathcal D\bigr\}\subset\mathbb R^N
\]
is compact and convex. Moreover, the \(L^1\)-continuity of Gaussian translations gives
\[
 \sup_{\delta\in\mathcal D}|q_{\delta}(h)-q_{\delta}(h')|
 \leq\int|\varphi_{\Sigma}(z-h)-\varphi_{\Sigma}(z-h')|\,dz\longrightarrow0
\]
as \(h'\to h\). Together with uniform continuity of \(c_{+}\) and \(c_{-}\), this proves that \(s\mapsto r_s(\delta)\) is equicontinuous over \(\delta\in\mathcal D\).

For completeness, consider first a finite state set \(T=\{s_1,\ldots,s_N\}\). Let \(C\) be the compact convex risk-vector set just displayed and put
\[
 t_T=\min_{x\in C}\max_{1\leq i\leq N}x_i.
\]
The following elementary finite-dimensional separation argument yields
\[
 t_T=\max_{a\in\Delta_N}\min_{x\in C}\sum_{i=1}^Na_ix_i. \tag{1}
\]
For \(\epsilon>0\), the compact set \(C\) and the closed lower orthant \(O_{\epsilon}=\{y:y_i\leq t_T-\epsilon\ \forall i\}\) are disjoint. Choose a closest pair. The vector joining the pair separates the two convex sets; because \(O_{\epsilon}\) is unbounded in every negative coordinate direction, every coordinate of the separating normal is nonnegative. Normalize its coordinates to sum to one and let \(\epsilon\downarrow0\). Compactness of \(\Delta_N\) gives \(a\in\Delta_N\) with \(\min_{x\in C}a^{\top}x\geq t_T\). The reverse inequality follows from \(a^{\top}x\leq\max_i x_i\). This proves (1).

Choose nested finite sets \(T_m\subset S\) with dense union and let \(t_m=t_{T_m}\). Compactness of \(S\) and the equicontinuity proved above imply that there is \(e_m\downarrow0\) such that
\[
 0\leq R(\delta)-\max_{s\in T_m}r_s(\delta)\leq e_m
 \qquad\text{for every }\delta\in\mathcal D. \tag{2}
\]
It follows that \(t_m\uparrow v\). Let \(\delta_m\) minimize the finite problem. A weak \(L^2(\mu)\) subsequential limit \(\delta^{\star}\in\mathcal D\) satisfies \(r_s(\delta^{\star})\leq v\) first for every \(s\) in the dense union and then, by continuity in \(s\), for every \(s\in S\). Hence \(R(\delta^{\star})=v\), so the primal minimum is attained.

Define the bilinear payoff
\[
 \mathcal L(\delta,\pi)=\int_S r_s(\delta)\,d\pi(s).
\]
For any \(\pi\in\Pi\), boundedness permits Tonelli's theorem and gives
\[
 \mathcal L(\delta,\pi)
 =\int_Hc_{+}(h)\,d\pi(h,+)
   +\int_{\mathbb R^p}\delta(z)\{A_{\pi,-}(z)-A_{\pi,+}(z)\}\,dz. \tag{3}
\]
Pointwise minimization over \(0\leq\delta\leq1\) in (3) yields
\[
 \min_{\delta\in\mathcal D}\mathcal L(\delta,\pi)
 =\int_{\mathbb R^p}\min\{A_{\pi,+}(z),A_{\pi,-}(z)\}\,dz=b(\pi). \tag{4}
\]
The minimum is attained, and the nonnegative pointwise excess in (3) vanishes exactly when
\[
 \delta=1\ \text{on }\{B_{\pi}>0\},\qquad
 \delta=0\ \text{on }\{B_{\pi}<0\}, \tag{5}
\]
with arbitrary values on \(\{B_{\pi}=0\}\). Thus (5) proves, rather than assumes, the asserted Bayes-response characterization.

For each finite \(T_m\), equations (1) and (4) give a prior \(\pi_m\) supported on \(T_m\) with \(b(\pi_m)=t_m\). Probability measures on the compact metric space \(S\) are sequentially compact for weak convergence: one direct proof takes successively finer finite Borel partitions with null boundaries, extracts a diagonal subsequence of all cell masses, and extends the consistent limiting masses to a probability measure. Let \(\pi_m\) converge along such a subsequence to \(\pi^{\star}\). For fixed \(\delta\), continuity of \(s\mapsto r_s(\delta)\) gives continuity of \(\pi\mapsto\mathcal L(\delta,\pi)\). Therefore \(b=\inf_{\delta}\mathcal L(\delta,\cdot)\) is upper semicontinuous, so
\[
 b(\pi^{\star})\geq\limsup_m b(\pi_m)=v. \tag{6}
\]
Weak duality, obtained from \(b(\pi)\leq\mathcal L(\delta,\pi)\leq R(\delta)\), gives \(b(\pi)\leq v\) for every \(\pi\). Thus equality holds in (6), the dual maximum is attained, and
\[
 v=\min_{\delta\in\mathcal D}\max_{s\in S}r_s(\delta)
  =\max_{\pi\in\Pi}b(\pi). \tag{7}
\]

We next characterize every saddle. If \((\delta,\pi)\) is a saddle, its payoff equals the common value in (7). Minimization against \(\pi\) and (4) imply the sign rule (5). Maximization against \(\delta\) implies \(r_s(\delta)\leq v\) for every \(s\). Finally,
\[
 0=v-\mathcal L(\delta,\pi)=\int_S\{v-r_s(\delta)\}\,d\pi(s),
\]
whose integrand is nonnegative; hence \(r_s(\delta)=v\) for \(\pi\)-almost every \(s\). Conversely, the three displayed conditions imply by (4) that \(b(\pi)=\mathcal L(\delta,\pi)=v\), while the global inequalities imply \(R(\delta)=v\). For arbitrary \(\delta'\) and \(\pi'\),
\[
 \mathcal L(\delta,\pi')\leq R(\delta)=v
 =b(\pi)\leq\mathcal L(\delta',\pi),
\]
so the pair is a saddle.

The set \(\mathcal D^{\star}\) is nonempty by primal attainment and convex because \(R\), a supremum of affine maps, is convex. The set \(\Pi^{\star}\) is nonempty by dual attainment and convex because \(b\), an infimum of affine maps of \(\pi\), is concave. If \(\delta\in\mathcal D^{\star}\) and \(\pi\in\Pi^{\star}\), then
\[
 v=b(\pi)\leq\mathcal L(\delta,\pi)\leq R(\delta)=v,
\]
so every such pair is a saddle.

Finally, \(\mathfrak F^{\star}\) is finite because the two endpoints have finitely many affine pieces. If it is nonempty, choose \(\pi_F\) as in \(\mathrm{def:face-complete-prior}\) for every \(F\in\mathfrak F^{\star}\), and set
\[
 \bar\pi=|\mathfrak F^{\star}|^{-1}\sum_{F\in\mathfrak F^{\star}}\pi_F.
\]
Convexity of \(\Pi^{\star}\) puts \(\bar\pi\) in \(\Pi^{\star}\), and every required relative interior receives positive \(\bar\pi\)-mass. Thus \(\bar\pi\in\Pi^{\mathrm{fc}}\). If \(\mathfrak F^{\star}=\varnothing\), the defining face-completeness requirement is vacuous and every member of the nonempty set \(\Pi^{\star}\) belongs to \(\Pi^{\mathrm{fc}}\).

statements.statement: For the exchange construction in \(\mathrm{def:exchange-certificate}\), \(L_m\le v\le U_m\) at every iteration, \(L_m\uparrow v\), and \(G_m\to0\). Every weak limit point of \(\pi_m\) lies in \(\Pi^{\star}\). Regard each \(\delta_m\) as its \(\lambda^p\)-almost-everywhere equivalence class in \(\mathcal D\subset L^{\infty}(\lambda^p)\); every cluster point in the weak-star topology \(\sigma(L^{\infty}(\lambda^p),L^1(\lambda^p))\) along a subsequence with \(G_m\to0\) lies in \(\mathcal D^{\star}\). These conclusions make no iteration-complexity or convergence-rate claim.
statements.justification: The proposition turns the analytic saddle theorem into checkable global upper and lower certificates and places selector convergence in the weak-star compact topology of the unrestricted \(L^{\infty}\) rule space.

statements.proof_tex:
Let
\[
 v_m=\min_{\delta\in\mathcal D}\max_{s\in S_m}r_s(\delta).
\]
The restricted saddle chosen in \(\mathrm{def:exchange-certificate}\) and the finite-state separation argument in \(\mathrm{thm:complete-saddle-duality}\) give
\[
 L_m=b(\pi_m)=v_m=\max_{s\in S_m}r_s(\delta_m). \tag{1}
\]
Weak duality and the definition of \(U_m\) therefore yield
\[
 L_m\leq v\leq U_m. \tag{2}
\]
Because \(S_m\subseteq S_{m+1}\), the values \(v_m=L_m\) are nondecreasing.

Equip the compact set \(S\) with any compatible metric that separates its two sign components, and put
\[
 d_m=\sup_{s\in S}\inf_{t\in S_m}d_S(s,t).
\]
The nested meshes contain successive points of a dense sequence, so compactness of \(S\) gives \(d_m\to0\). As established equation by equation in \(\mathrm{thm:complete-saddle-duality}\), continuity of the endpoint weights and \(L^1\)-continuity of Gaussian translations imply a deterministic modulus \(\zeta(t)\downarrow0\) such that
\[
 |r_s(\delta)-r_t(\delta)|\leq\zeta(d_S(s,t))
 \quad\text{for all }s,t\text{ with the same sign and every }\delta\in\mathcal D.
\]
Consequently, for all sufficiently large \(m\) (and this is all that is needed for the limit),
\[
 0\leq U_m-L_m
 =R(\delta_m)-\max_{s\in S_m}r_s(\delta_m)
 \leq\zeta(d_m). \tag{3}
\]
Equations (2)--(3) prove \(G_m\to0\) and \(L_m\uparrow v\).

Suppose \(\pi_{m_j}\Rightarrow\bar\pi\). For fixed \(\delta\), the map \(\pi\mapsto\int r_s(\delta)\,d\pi(s)\) is weakly continuous. Hence \(b\), its infimum over \(\delta\), is upper semicontinuous. Using \(b(\pi_{m_j})=L_{m_j}\to v\) and weak duality,
\[
 v\geq b(\bar\pi)\geq\limsup_j b(\pi_{m_j})=v,
\]
so \(\bar\pi\in\Pi^{\star}\).

Now suppose that \(\delta_{m_j}\to\bar\delta\) in \(\sigma(L^{\infty}(\lambda^p),L^1(\lambda^p))\) and \(G_{m_j}\to0\). Each \(r_s\) is weak-star continuous because its only rule-dependent term is integration against the \(L^1\) density \(\varphi_{\Sigma}(\,\cdot-h)\). Therefore \(R=\sup_s r_s\) is weak-star lower semicontinuous, and
\[
 R(\bar\delta)\leq\liminf_jR(\delta_{m_j})
 =\liminf_jU_{m_j}=v.
\]
The definition of \(v\) gives the reverse inequality. Thus \(R(\bar\delta)=v\), so \(\bar\delta\in\mathcal D^{\star}\). No step bounds \(d_m\) as a function of \(m\), so the argument asserts neither an iteration complexity nor a convergence rate.

statements.proof_tex:
For the game \(\mathsf G_{\nu}\), let \(L\) and \(U\) be the certified dual lower and primal upper values. Weak duality from \(\mathrm{thm:complete-saddle-duality}\) gives
\[
 L\leq v_{\nu}\leq U=R_{\nu}(\widetilde\delta_{\nu}).
\]
The certificate and strict positivity required by \(\mathrm{def:stable-selector}\) give \(U-L\leq\varepsilon_{\nu}\), whence
\[
 0\leq R_{\nu}(\widetilde\delta_{\nu})-v_{\nu}
 \leq U-L\leq\varepsilon_{\nu}.
\]
At exchange iteration \(m\), \(U_m=R(\delta_m)\), \(L_m\leq v\), and \(G_m=U_m-L_m\), so the identical subtraction gives \(0\leq R(\delta_m)-v\leq G_m\). This is purely the primal--dual gap implication; no continuity or limiting assertion is used.

statements.statement: The construction in \(\mathrm{def:coexistence-witness}\) is a legal member of \(\mathcal G_2\) but not of \(\mathcal G_2^{\mathrm{cs}}\), because \(H_0\ne-H_0\). Its minimax value is \(v=2/3\). The constant rule \(\delta_0\) belongs to \(\mathcal D^{\star}\cap\mathcal D_1\). For every \(0<\eta\le1/2\), the rule \(\delta_{\eta}\) belongs to \(\mathcal D^{\star}\setminus\mathcal D_1\). Therefore \(\mathcal G_2^{\mathrm{cs}}\subsetneq\mathcal G_2\), and the witness game lies in \(\mathsf C_{\mathrm{co}}\).
statements.justification: This proposition verifies the presolve value, proves the strict internal inclusion \(\mathcal G_2^{\mathrm{cs}}\subsetneq\mathcal G_2\), and shows why existence of one optimal index rule cannot classify the full correspondence.

statements.proof_tex:
The triangle \(H_0\) is compact, convex, and has nonempty interior, and \(I_2\) is positive definite. Convexity of the unit \(\ell_{\infty}\)-ball and the fact that all three vertices have \(\ell_{\infty}\)-norm one imply
\[
 \|h\|_{\infty}\leq1\qquad(h\in H_0). \tag{1}
\]
The functions \(\ell_0\) and \(u_0\) are respectively a finite maximum and a finite minimum of affine functions, since
\[
 \ell_0(h)=\max_{\substack{i=1,2\\ \sigma\in\{-1,1\}}}\{-4/3+\sigma h_i\},
 \qquad
 u_0(h)=\min_{\substack{i=1,2\\ \sigma\in\{-1,1\}}}\{4/3-\sigma h_i\}.
\]
By (1), \(\ell_0(h)\leq-1/3<1/3\leq u_0(h)\). Also
\(0=\tfrac14(-1,-1)+\tfrac14(1,-1)+\tfrac12(0,1)\), so at \(h=0\) the interval strictly straddles zero. Thus all member conditions in \(\mathrm{def:game-class}\) hold. The point \((-1,1)=-(1,-1)\) is not in \(H_0\), because the only point of \(H_0\) with second coordinate one is \((0,1)\). Hence \(H_0\neq-H_0\), so the game is not in \(\mathcal G_2^{\mathrm{cs}}\).

By (1), both loss weights equal
\[
 c_{+}(h)=c_{-}(h)=c(h):=4/3-\|h\|_{\infty}. \tag{2}
\]
At \(h=0\), for every rule \(\delta\),
\[
 \max\{r_{(0,+)}(\delta),r_{(0,-)}(\delta)\}
 =\frac43\max\{1-q_{\delta}(0),q_{\delta}(0)\}\geq\frac23. \tag{3}
\]
The constant rule has \(q_{\delta_0}(h)=1/2\), so (2) gives \(R(\delta_0)\leq2/3\). Equation (3) proves \(v=2/3\) and \(\delta_0\in\mathcal D^{\star}\). It belongs to \(\mathcal D_1\): take any nonzero \(w\) and the constant Borel map \(g\equiv1/2\).

Let \(X\sim N(0,1)\) and define \(f(t)=E[\tanh(t+X)]\). Symmetry of \(X\) and oddness of \(\tanh\) make \(f\) odd. Dominated differentiation gives
\[
 f'(t)=E[\operatorname{sech}^2(t+X)]\in(0,1],
\]
so \(f\) has the sign of \(t\) and \(|f(t)|\leq|t|\). Independence of the coordinates under \(N(h,I_2)\) yields
\[
 q_{\delta_{\eta}}(h)=\frac12+\eta f(h_1)f(h_2). \tag{4}
\]
Put \(r=\|h\|_{\infty}\leq1\). From (2)--(4), \(0<\eta\leq1/2\), and \(|h_1h_2|\leq r^2\), either signed risk is at most
\[
 (4/3-r)\left(\frac12+\frac12r^2\right)\leq\frac23. \tag{5}
\]
Indeed, after multiplying by two, the difference between the left side and \(4/3\) equals
\[
 r\left(\frac43r-1-r^2\right)<0\quad(0<r\leq1),
\]
because \(r^2-4r/3+1>0\); equality holds at \(r=0\). Thus \(R(\delta_{\eta})=2/3\), so \(\delta_{\eta}\in\mathcal D^{\star}\).

It remains to exclude a one-index representation. Suppose
\(\delta_{\eta}(z)=g(w^{\top}z)\) almost everywhere for \(w=(w_1,w_2)\neq0\), and put \(e=(-w_2,w_1)\). For every fixed \(t\), translation invariance of Lebesgue null sets gives
\(\delta_{\eta}(z+te)=\delta_{\eta}(z)\) almost everywhere. Both sides are continuous in \(z\), hence the equality holds everywhere. Differentiating at \(t=0\) gives
\[
 -w_2\operatorname{sech}^2(z_1)\tanh(z_2)
 +w_1\tanh(z_1)\operatorname{sech}^2(z_2)=0
 \qquad(z\in\mathbb R^2). \tag{6}
\]
Setting \(z_1=0\) in (6) gives \(w_2=0\), and setting \(z_2=0\) gives \(w_1=0\), a contradiction. Therefore \(\delta_{\eta}\notin\mathcal D_1\). The two optimal rules establish \(\mathsf C_{\mathrm{co}}\), and the exhibited member outside \(\mathcal G_2^{\mathrm{cs}}\) proves \(\mathcal G_2^{\mathrm{cs}}\subsetneq\mathcal G_2\).

statements.statement:
The actual compact-polyhedral overlap with Theorem 4 of \cite{MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Local} is a proper subclass of the proposed two-dimensional regime:
\[
\mathcal O_2^{(4)}\subsetneq\mathcal G_2.
\]
The inclusion follows from \(\mathcal O_2^{(4)}\subseteq\mathcal G_2^{\mathrm{cs}}\subseteq\mathcal G_2\), while strictness is certified by the triangular game in \(\mathrm{prop:coexistence-witness}\), which belongs to \(\mathcal G_2\) but not to \(\mathcal G_2^{\mathrm{cs}}\), and hence not to \(\mathcal O_2^{(4)}\). Thus \(\mathrm{thm:complete-saddle-duality}\) applies both to every game in the compact-polyhedral overlap and to at least one asymmetric game outside that overlap. No inclusion between \(\mathcal G_p\) and the full published Assumption-5 class is asserted.
statements.justification: The proposition proves the only strict-extension statement used in the proposal: the new two-dimensional class strictly contains the actual compact-polyhedral Theorem 4 overlap, with strictness supplied by an explicit asymmetric game.
statements.gap: Assumption 5 with Theorem 4 of \cite{MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Local} covers a directionally differentiable centrosymmetric class. This proposition compares only on the defined compact-polyhedral overlap and does not claim that the proposed class contains the full published Assumption-5 class.
statements.consumer: Researchers can identify exactly when the published centered solver is in scope and when the asymmetric all-saddle analysis supplies genuinely additional admissible games.
statements.proof_tex:
By \(\mathrm{def:theorem4-overlap}\), every element of \(\mathcal O_2^{(4)}\) is an element of \(\mathcal G_2^{\mathrm{cs}}\), and by \(\mathrm{def:centrosymmetric-comparator-class}\), every element of \(\mathcal G_2^{\mathrm{cs}}\) is an element of \(\mathcal G_2\). Hence
\[
 \mathcal O_2^{(4)}\subseteq\mathcal G_2^{\mathrm{cs}}\subseteq\mathcal G_2. \tag{1}
\]
The game in \(\mathrm{def:coexistence-witness}\) belongs to \(\mathcal G_2\) by \(\mathrm{prop:coexistence-witness}\), whereas its triangular domain satisfies \(H_0\neq-H_0\), so it does not belong to \(\mathcal G_2^{\mathrm{cs}}\). By (1) it cannot belong to \(\mathcal O_2^{(4)}\). Thus the first inclusion into \(\mathcal G_2\) is proper. Application of \(\mathrm{thm:complete-saddle-duality}\) to every member of \(\mathcal G_2\) then covers both every game in \(\mathcal O_2^{(4)}\) and this explicit asymmetric game. The proof compares only the two sets in (1), so it entails no relation between \(\mathcal G_p\) and the full published Assumption-5 class.

statements.statement: Can \(\mathscr H_{\mathrm{idx}}\) be completed into a finite, non-tautological necessary-and-sufficient criterion, stated only in the covariance-whitened endpoint-face normals, face incidence, and supports of face-complete least-favorable priors, that decides whether a game in \(\mathcal G_p\) lies in \(\mathsf C_{\mathrm{all}}\), \(\mathsf C_{\mathrm{co}}\), or \(\mathsf C_{\mathrm{none}}\)? The criterion must separately certify ridge factorization of every forced Bayes response and the presence or absence of non-ridge perturbations preserving all binding risks.
statements.justification: This exposes the non-tautological geometric classification as the central open content rather than confusing an exhibited index rule with factorization of all optima.
statements.gap: MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Decision proves multiplicity and excludes some threshold rules, while Yata2025Optimal exhibits one optimal index under symmetry; neither classifies the unrestricted optimal correspondence.
statements.consumer: A policy maker can learn whether reporting one scalar score is lossless, merely one admissible representation, or impossible for every minimax rule.

obligation.what_is_open: A finite necessary-and-sufficient classifier using only covariance-whitened endpoint-face normals, face incidence, and supports of face-complete least-favorable priors remains unproved.
obligation.obstruction: The frozen primitives give the full optimal correspondence through Bayes-score signs plus a continuum of binding Gaussian convolution inequalities. They contain no reduction showing that prior weights and those continuum moment constraints are determined by the requested finite support geometry, and no pair of games proving that such a reduction is impossible.
obligation.attempted: The complete saddle characterization was used with an arbitrary face-complete prior. This isolates the unique-score case and the tie-set perturbation case exactly, but compressing the latter's continuum of risk inequalities to the proposed normal-fan data would assume the central claim.
obligation.partial_result:
The proved saddle theorem gives the following exact, but generally infinite-dimensional, reduction. For any \(\pi_0\in\Pi^{\mathrm{fc}}\), every \(\delta\in\mathcal D^{\star}\) is a Bayes response to \(\pi_0\), and
\[
 \mathcal D^{\star}
 =\left\{\delta\in\mathcal D:
 \delta=1\text{ on }\{B_{\pi_0}>0\},\
 \delta=0\text{ on }\{B_{\pi_0}<0\},\
 r_s(\delta)\leq v\text{ for every }s\in S
 \right\}.
\]
In particular, if \(\lambda^p\{B_{\pi_0}=0\}=0\), the correspondence is a singleton, so only the all-one-index and no-one-index categories are possible, according as \(\mathbf1\{B_{\pi_0}>0\}\) does or does not factor through one linear projection. If the tie set has positive measure, all remaining freedom is a bounded perturbation supported on that tie set subject to the displayed binding-risk inequalities. This is a computable functional characterization once \(\pi_0\) is known, but it is not the requested finite criterion in normals, incidence, and supports alone.

statements.statement: Let \(p=2\), let \(\mathsf G\in\mathcal G_p\), and let \(\pi\in\Pi\) be finitely supported. If the finite curved-score certificate in \(\mathrm{def:curved-score-certificate}\) holds, then \(R(\delta_{\pi})=b(\pi)=v=q\), \(\pi\in\Pi^{\star}\), and \(\mathcal D^{\star}=\{\delta_{\pi}\}\) up to \(\lambda^p\)-almost-everywhere equality. Moreover, \(\delta_{\pi}\notin\mathcal D_1\), so \(\mathsf G\in\mathsf C_{\mathrm{none}}\). Thus exact primal-dual closure, nonvanishing of the finite Gaussian-mixture score, and one regular boundary arc with curvature bounded away from zero form a finite sufficient certificate for the no-one-index branch.
statements.justification: This is the new angle's theorem-level kernel: it turns a finite-support prior, a closed global regret gap, and a local two-jet calculation into uniqueness over all measurable randomized rules and impossibility of every scalar-index representation.
statements.gap: MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Decision excludes linear threshold rules only under special conditions and does not exclude arbitrary randomized one-index rules. Theorems 1--2 of AradillasFernandezMontielOleaQiuStoyeTinda2026RobustBayes characterize uniqueness, randomization, and linear-index threshold behavior for ex-ante and ex-post robust-Bayes criteria under the constrained prior class in their equation (2.9); they do not characterize the unrestricted minimax-regret saddle over all endpoint states or exclude every measurable rule of the form \(g(w^{\top}z)\). The Abstract of the corrected proof of ChristensenMoonSchorfheide2026OptimalDecisionRules states an asymptotic discrete-choice criterion that combines minimax treatment of ambiguity in the partially identified payoff parameter conditional on a point-identified parameter with average-risk minimization for that point-identified parameter. That hybrid asymptotic criterion neither implies nor is implied by exact minimax regret over every signed endpoint state, and the cited abstract makes no claim excluding every arbitrary measurable one-index rule. ZahmEtAl2020Ridge characterizes ridge approximation through projections, but not exact minimax decision correspondences or curved Gaussian-mixture Bayes boundaries.
statements.consumer: A researcher can validate one finite certificate and conclude that every minimax treatment rule must use genuinely multivariate data, without searching the unrestricted rule space for alternative index representations.
statements.proof_tex:
Write \(\mathcal L(\delta,\pi)=\int r_s(\delta)\,d\pi(s)\). Weak duality from \(\mathrm{thm:complete-saddle-duality}\) gives, for the certified pair,
\[
 b(\pi)\leq v\leq R(\delta_{\pi}). \tag{1}
\]
The certificate in \(\mathrm{def:curved-score-certificate}\) gives
\(R(\delta_{\pi})\leq q\leq b(\pi)\). Combining with (1) forces
\[
 R(\delta_{\pi})=q=b(\pi)=v. \tag{2}
\]
Thus \(\delta_{\pi}\in\mathcal D^{\star}\), \(\pi\in\Pi^{\star}\), and the pair is a saddle.

We next show that its Bayes response is unique almost everywhere. After combining atoms having the same mean, the finite score can be written
\[
 B_{\pi}(z)=\varphi_{\Sigma}(z)
 \sum_{i=1}^N d_i
 \exp\!\left(h_i^{\top}\Sigma^{-1}z-\frac12h_i^{\top}\Sigma^{-1}h_i\right), \tag{3}
\]
where the \(h_i\)'s are distinct and every remaining \(d_i\neq0\). The certificate says that (3) is not identically zero. Choose a vector \(e\) outside the finitely many hyperplanes
\(\{e:e^{\top}\Sigma^{-1}(h_i-h_j)=0\}\). On every affine line \(x+te\), the second factor in (3) is a linear combination of exponentials with distinct real exponents and nonzero coefficients. Such a combination has at most \(N-1\) zeros, counting multiplicities: divide by the smallest exponential, differentiate, and apply Rolle's theorem inductively. Fubini's theorem therefore gives
\[
 \lambda^2\{z:B_{\pi}(z)=0\}=0. \tag{4}
\]
Every \(\delta\in\mathcal D^{\star}\) forms a saddle with this \(\pi\) by \(\mathrm{thm:complete-saddle-duality}\). Its Bayes-response characterization then fixes \(\delta=1\) on \(\{B_{\pi}>0\}\) and \(\delta=0\) on \(\{B_{\pi}<0\}\). Equation (4) proves \(\delta=\delta_{\pi}\) almost everywhere. Hence \(\mathcal D^{\star}=\{\delta_{\pi}\}\) modulo \(\lambda^2\)-null sets.

It remains to rule out every measurable one-index representation. Let \(\Omega=\{B_{\pi}>0\}\), so \(\delta_{\pi}=\mathbf1_{\Omega}\). Suppose, to the contrary, that \(\mathbf1_{\Omega}(z)=g(w^{\top}z)\) almost everywhere for some \(w\neq0\), and choose a nonzero \(e\perp w\). For every \(t\in\mathbb R\),
\[
 \mathbf1_{\Omega}(z+te)=\mathbf1_{\Omega}(z)\quad\text{for almost every }z. \tag{5}
\]
Equation (5) says that the distributional derivative of \(\mathbf1_{\Omega}\) in direction \(e\) is zero: translate a compactly supported smooth test function, integrate, and differentiate at zero. On a neighborhood of any point of the regular arc \(\Gamma\), the implicit-function theorem and \(\nabla B_{\pi}\neq0\) identify the distributional boundary measure of \(\Omega\) as its ordinary \(C^1\) boundary measure with unit normal
\[
 n(z)=\frac{\nabla B_{\pi}(z)}{\|\nabla B_{\pi}(z)\|}.
\]
Integration by parts against test functions supported in that neighborhood turns the zero distributional derivative into \(e^{\top}n(z)=0\) for boundary-almost every \(z\in\Gamma\). Continuity of \(n\) upgrades this equality to every \(z\in\Gamma\). Hence the normal is everywhere parallel to the fixed vector \(w\), so the tangent is everywhere parallel to the fixed vector \(e\). The connected arc \(\Gamma\) is therefore contained in an affine line.

Let \(T(z)=(-\partial_2B_{\pi}(z),\partial_1B_{\pi}(z))\), a nonzero tangent to the regular level set. Along a straight level-set arc, twice differentiating \(B_{\pi}(z+te)=0\) gives \(e^{\top}\nabla^2B_{\pi}(z)e=0\). Since \(T\) is a nonzero multiple of \(e\),
\[
 \mathcal K_{\pi}(z)=T(z)^{\top}\nabla^2B_{\pi}(z)T(z)=0
 \qquad(z\in\Gamma),
\]
contradicting the certified strictly positive lower bound for \(|\mathcal K_{\pi}|\). Thus \(\delta_{\pi}\notin\mathcal D_1\). Uniqueness then gives \(\mathcal D^{\star}\cap\mathcal D_1=\varnothing\), which is \(\mathsf C_{\mathrm{none}}\) by \(\mathrm{def:indexability-categories}\).

statements.statement: Does there exist a game in \(\mathcal G_p\) with \(p=2\), rational vertices of \(H\), rational entries of \(\Sigma\), rational endpoint intercepts and normals, and a finite prior \(\pi\in\Pi^{\mathrm{fc}}\) having rational support points, rational masses, and unequal total masses on the two endpoint signs, such that the finite curved-score certificate holds for \(\delta_{\pi}\); or are these requirements impossible in two dimensions? An affirmative certificate must instantiate \(\mathscr H_{\mathrm{noidx}}\): give a rational \(q\), finite rational box partitions, outward-rounded interval enclosures, and analytic Gaussian-tail bounds proving \(R(\delta_{\pi})\le q\le b(\pi)\). It must also enclose \(B_{\pi}\), its first two derivatives, and \(\mathcal K_{\pi}\) on a rational box meeting a nondegenerate arc \(\Gamma\subset\mathcal Z_{\pi}\), with strictly positive rational lower bounds on the score-gradient norm and on \( |\mathcal K_{\pi}|\), and certify \(B_{\pi}\not\equiv0\). The conclusion \(R(\delta_{\pi})=b(\pi)=v=q\), uniqueness almost everywhere, and \(\mathcal D^{\star}\cap\mathcal D_1=\varnothing\) must then follow through \(\mathrm{thm:curved-score-no-index-certificate}\), rather than being assumed.
statements.justification: This is the early kill test for the no-one-index branch and demands finite rational data, exact primal-dual closure, and a reproducible interval-arithmetic curvature certificate rather than a numerical plot.
statements.gap: Tetenov2012Asymmetric retains threshold structure in point-identified asymmetric problems, and the known partial-identification examples do not certify an unbalanced globally minimax non-halfspace rule.
statements.consumer: A certified example would establish that multivariate reporting is sometimes intrinsically necessary; an impossibility theorem would sharply simplify the classification program.

obligation.what_is_open: Neither an explicit rational unbalanced-prior interval certificate nor a two-dimensional impossibility theorem is present in, or derivable from, the frozen primitives.
obligation.obstruction: The question requires concrete rational support and mass data, outward-rounded enclosures of global Gaussian integrals and derivatives, a rational truncation and tail bound, and exact primal--dual closure. No such numerical candidate or enclosure is supplied, so inventing one would not be a proof.
obligation.attempted: The algebraic closure and geometric implication were separated and proved in \(\mathrm{thm:curved-score-no-index-certificate}\). The available triangular game was also checked, but it proves coexistence through a balanced equalizer and does not instantiate the demanded unbalanced curved-score certificate.
obligation.partial_result: The proved curved-score theorem reduces an affirmative example to finite rational data plus two independently checkable certificates: the global inequalities \(R(\delta_{\pi})\leq q\leq b(\pi)\), and one rational box intersecting a regular score-zero arc on which interval enclosures keep both \(\|\nabla B_{\pi}\|\) and \(|\mathcal K_{\pi}|\) strictly positive. Once those inequalities are supplied, weak duality forces exact equality and the finite Gaussian-mixture argument proves uniqueness and failure of every measurable one-index representation. The frozen core, however, contains no candidate rational game, prior, partition, truncation box, interval enclosure, or Gaussian-tail remainder from which either the affirmative certificate or a two-dimensional impossibility theorem can be derived.

statements.justification: The explicit primitive-game modulus controls values and certified rules, while the nonstandard two-sided experiment-equivalence premise, separate almost-sure legality and numerical boundedness, and joint total-variation premise control every bounded endpoint loss; multiplicity and active-face changes therefore do not invalidate the conditional feasible transfer.
statements.gap: Theorem 3 of MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Local gives the feasible fully differentiable rule, while Assumption 5 and Theorem 5 give feasible transfer for its directionally differentiable centrosymmetric rule. HiranoPorter2009 motivates pointwise limit-experiment treatment-rule analysis but does not supply the compact-\(H\), two-sided total-variation equivalence or the joint approximation with an estimated game assumed here. The present theorem conditionally treats the non-centrosymmetric polyhedral class and quantifies perturbation error uniformly over saddle and indexability ties; FangSantos2019 and FirpoGalvaoParker2023 explain why pointwise plug-in reasoning alone is insufficient at such nonsmooth boundaries.
statements.consumer: Researchers estimating covariance and bound derivatives obtain a feasible treatment rule whose regret guarantee remains valid near face and indexability boundaries.
statements.proof_tex:
We first prove the deterministic modulus. Write \(\mathsf G'=(H',\Sigma',\ell',u')\), suppose both \(\mathsf B_{\kappa}(\mathsf G)\) and \(\mathsf B_{\kappa}(\mathsf G')\) hold, and put \(\rho=d_{\mathsf G}(\mathsf G',\mathsf G)\leq(2\kappa)^{-1}\). Every endpoint loss weight in either game is bounded by
\[
 \kappa+\kappa^2=M_{\kappa}, \tag{1}
\]
because every mean has norm at most \(\kappa\), and every affine intercept and normal has magnitude or norm at most \(\kappa\).

Fix a signed state \((h',\sigma)\) of \(\mathsf G'\). Hausdorff distance at most \(\rho\) between the corresponding endpoint graphs supplies a state \((h,\sigma)\) of \(\mathsf G\) such that
\[
 \|h'-h\|\leq\rho,
 \qquad |c'_{\sigma}(h')-c_{\sigma}(h)|\leq\rho, \tag{2}
\]
where the second inequality uses the fact that the positive-part map is one-Lipschitz. Put \(E=\Sigma^{-1/2}(\Sigma'-\Sigma)\Sigma^{-1/2}\). The eigenvalue bound and the definition of \(d_{\mathsf G}\) give
\(\|E\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq\kappa\rho\leq1/2\). Direct integration of the two Gaussian densities gives
\[
 D_{\mathrm{KL}}\{N(h',\Sigma')\|N(h,\Sigma)\}
 =\frac12\left[\operatorname{tr}E-\log\det(I+E)
 +(h-h')^{\top}\Sigma^{-1}(h-h')\right]. \tag{3}
\]
For \(|x|\leq1/2\), \(x-\log(1+x)\leq2x^2\), as follows by differentiating the two sides. Thus (3) is at most
\[
 \rho^2\left(p\kappa^2+\frac\kappa2\right). \tag{4}
\]
The total-variation inequality used here follows directly from scalar convexity: applying the log-sum inequality to the set where the first density exceeds the second reduces relative entropy to binary relative entropy, and two differentiations show that binary relative entropy is at least twice the squared difference of its success probabilities. Therefore
\[
 \|P-Q\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\leq\sqrt{D_{\mathrm{KL}}(P\|Q)/2}.
\]
Together with (4), this gives
\[
 \|N(h',\Sigma')-N(h,\Sigma)\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \leq\rho\sqrt{p\kappa^2/2+\kappa/4}. \tag{5}
\]
For every \(0\leq\delta\leq1\), differences of expectations are bounded by total variation. Equations (1), (2), and (5) therefore imply, for the matched signed states,
\[
 |r'_{(h',\sigma)}(\delta)-r_{(h,\sigma)}(\delta)|
 \leq\rho+M_{\kappa}\rho\sqrt{p\kappa^2/2+\kappa/4}
 =\omega_{p,\kappa}(\rho). \tag{6}
\]
Repeating the graph matching in the opposite direction and taking suprema proves
\[
 \sup_{\delta\in\mathcal D}|R'(\delta)-R(\delta)|
 \leq\omega_{p,\kappa}(\rho). \tag{7}
\]
Taking infima in (7) gives \(|v'-v|\leq\omega_{p,\kappa}(\rho)\). For larger \(\rho\), both signed risks lie in \([0,M_{\kappa}]\), so the same two conclusions hold with the extended modulus \(\overline\omega_{p,\kappa}(\rho)=M_{\kappa}\).

Apply (7) to \(\mathsf G_{\nu}\). The gap lemma gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 R(\widetilde\delta_{\nu})-v
 &\leq |R(\widetilde\delta_{\nu})-R_{\nu}(\widetilde\delta_{\nu})|
 +(R_{\nu}(\widetilde\delta_{\nu})-v_{\nu})+|v_{\nu}-v|\\
 &\leq2\omega_{p,\kappa}(\rho_{\nu})+\varepsilon_{\nu}.
\end{aligned}\tag{8}
\]
The derivation uses neither uniqueness nor constancy of active faces, so it is uniform across every saddle, face, and indexability tie.

We turn to the original experiment. The almost-sure legality and boundedness assertions follow separately from \(\mathrm{ass:estimated-game-legality}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:estimated-game-kappa-bounds}\). They also hold under \(Q_{n,h}\), because the definition of that law gives
\[
 \mathcal L_{Q_{n,h}}(\widehat{\mathsf G}_n)
 =\mathcal L_{P_{n,h}}(\widehat{\mathsf G}_n). \tag{9}
\]
Condition on a realized legal game \(G'=\widehat{\mathsf G}_n\), and let \(d_{G'}\) be the certified rule chosen at tolerance \(\varepsilon_n>0\). Under \(Q_{n,h}\), its signal has law \(N(h,\widehat\Sigma_n)\). Match the true signed state \((h,\sigma)\) to the corresponding endpoint graph of \(G'\). The proof of (6), now with covariance \(\widehat\Sigma_n\) on both sides of this single state comparison, bounds the conditional true signed loss by the matching risk in \(G'\) plus \(\overline\omega_{p,\kappa}(d_{\mathsf G}(G',\mathsf G))\). The gap lemma and the value part of (7) then give, for either sign,
\[
 \operatorname{loss}_{Q_{n,h}}(h,\sigma\mid G')
 \leq v+\varepsilon_n
 +2\overline\omega_{p,\kappa}(d_{\mathsf G}(G',\mathsf G)). \tag{10}
\]
The common marginal in (9) and the definition of \(\alpha_n\) imply, after averaging (10),
\[
 \sup_{h\in H}\max_{\sigma\in\{+,-\}}
 \operatorname{loss}_{Q_{n,h}}(h,\sigma)
 \leq v+\varepsilon_n+2\alpha_n. \tag{11}
\]
Each loss integrand is between zero and \(M_{\kappa}\). The joint total-variation premise \(\mathrm{ass:joint-risk-transfer}\) therefore transfers (11) to the actual joint law at cost at most \(M_{\kappa}\gamma_n\), proving
\[
 \mathcal R_n^{\mathrm{loc}}(\widehat\delta_n)-v
 \leq\varepsilon_n+2\alpha_n+M_{\kappa}\gamma_n. \tag{12}
\]

For the lower bound, take any feasible original-experiment decision \(d:\mathcal X_n\to[0,1]\), including any auxiliary randomization through its conditional treatment probability, and compose it with the reverse kernel:
\[
 \delta_d(z)=\int_{\mathcal X_n}d(x)L_n(dx\mid z).
\]
This is a member of \(\mathcal D\). The reverse half of \(\mathrm{ass:uniform-two-sided-experiment-equivalence}\) and (1) imply, state by state,
\[
 r_s(\delta_d)\leq r^{\mathrm{orig}}_{n,s}(d)+M_{\kappa}\lambda_n.
\]
Here \(r^{\mathrm{orig}}_{n,(h,+)}(d)=c_{+}(h)\{1-E_{P_{n,h}}d\}\) and \(r^{\mathrm{orig}}_{n,(h,-)}(d)=c_{-}(h)E_{P_{n,h}}d\), so their supremum is exactly \(\mathcal R_n^{\mathrm{loc}}(d)\).
Taking the supremum over \(s\), then using \(v\leq R(\delta_d)\), yields
\[
 \mathcal R_n^{\mathrm{loc}}(d)-v\geq-M_{\kappa}\lambda_n. \tag{13}
\]
Apply (13) to \(d=\widehat\delta_n\) and combine it with (12). If \(\varepsilon_n\to0\) through strictly positive tolerances and \(\alpha_n+\gamma_n+\lambda_n\to0\), the two bounds squeeze \(\mathcal R_n^{\mathrm{loc}}(\widehat\delta_n)-v\) to zero. No step supplies a rate for any of these externally controlled error sequences.
